easy.def: One of the bones in your chest.
examples: I hurt my rib.
Ribs protect your heart.
A rib is a bone.

more.def: One of the long, curved bones that go around your chest.
examples: You have twelve pairs of ribs.
The ribs protect your heart and lungs.
He bruised a rib when he fell.

easy.def: A thin strip of cloth for tying or decorating.
examples: I tied a ribbon.
The ribbon is red.
She has a ribbon in her hair.

more.def: A long, narrow strip of cloth that is used for tying things or for decorating.
examples: She tied a ribbon around the gift.
I won a blue ribbon at the fair.
A pink ribbon was in her hair.

easy.def: The set of ribs in your chest.
examples: Your ribcage protects your heart.
The ribcage is bone.
She felt her ribcage.

more.def: The set of curved bones in your chest that protect your heart and lungs.
examples: Your ribcage protects your heart and lungs.
He took a deep breath and his ribcage expanded.
The doctor pointed to the ribcage on the X-ray.

easy.def: A soft white food that you cook in water.
examples: We eat rice with dinner.
The rice is hot.
I like fried rice.

more.def: Small, white or brown grains of a plant that are boiled or steamed and eaten.
examples: We had chicken and rice for dinner.
Rice grows in fields flooded with water.
Mom steamed a pot of rice.

easy.def: Having a lot of money.
examples: The rich king had gold.
She is rich.
The rich family lived in a big house.

more.def: Having a lot of money or valuable things.
examples: In the story, a rich king owned a golden castle.
The rich family lived in a huge mansion.
He worked hard and became rich.

easy.def: Strong in taste.
examples: A rich chocolate cake.
The soil is rich.
Rich soup is filling.

more.def: Full of flavor, or containing a lot of something good.
examples: The rich chocolate cake was very sweet.
Rich soil helps plants grow.
The milk was rich and creamy.

easy.def: A lot of money and valuable things.
examples: The pirate hid his riches.
Riches are gold.
The king had many riches.

more.def: Great wealth, such as money, gold and other valuable things.
examples: The pirate hid his riches in a cave.
The king had many riches and a huge castle.
The story is about a boy who found a map to great riches.

easy.def: In a splendid, deep way.
examples: The room was richly decorated.
She was richly dressed.
The cake was richly flavored.

more.def: In a deep, full or splendid way.
examples: The palace was richly decorated with gold.
The soup was richly flavored with spices.
She was richly rewarded for her work.

easy.def: Old and shaky.
examples: The rickety bridge swayed.
A rickety chair.
The rickety stairs creaked.

more.def: Weak and likely to break or fall apart.
examples: The rickety old bridge swayed in the wind.
A rickety chair wobbled when I sat on it.
The rickety stairs creaked under our feet.

easy.def: A small cart with two wheels pulled by a person.
examples: We rode in a rickshaw.
A rickshaw is pulled.
The rickshaw is small.

more.def: A light two-wheeled cart pulled by a person or a bicycle that carries passengers.
examples: We rode in a rickshaw through the busy streets.
The rickshaw driver pedaled hard.
A rickshaw can weave through traffic.

easy.def: To bounce off something.
examples: The ball will ricochet.
The stone ricocheted off the wall.
It ricocheted off the post.

more.def: To bounce off a surface and fly in another direction.
examples: The ball ricocheted off the wall.
A stone ricocheted across the pond.
The puck ricocheted off the post.

easy.def: To free from something you do not want.
examples: We got rid of the old toys.
He rid the garden of weeds.
How do I get rid of hiccups?

more.def: To free a place or person from something unwanted.
examples: The farmer wanted to rid the field of weeds.
We got rid of the old boxes.
A good wash will rid your hands of germs.

easy.def: A puzzling question with a clever answer.
examples: I told a riddle.
What is the answer to the riddle?
The riddle is funny.

more.def: A tricky question or puzzle that you answer by thinking in a clever way.
examples: I told my friend a riddle.
Can you guess the answer to the riddle?
The riddle asked what has hands but cannot clap.

easy.def: To sit on something and be carried along.
examples: I ride my bike.
We ride the bus to school.
She rode a horse.

more.def: To sit on or in something, such as a bike, a horse or a vehicle, as it carries you along.
examples: We rode the ferry across the bay to the island.
He rides his bike to the library on Saturdays.
Cowboys used to ride horses across the plains.

easy.def: A trip in a car or on a bike.
examples: Can I have a ride to school?
The bus ride was long.
We took a ride on the train.

more.def: A trip in a vehicle or on an animal.
examples: The ride to the airport took about forty minutes.
Dad gave my friend a ride home after practice.
The kids waited in line for a ride on the pony.

easy.def: A fun machine at a fair that carries you around.
examples: The Ferris wheel is my favorite ride.
I was too short for that ride.
This ride goes up very high.

more.def: A machine at a fair or amusement park that carries people around for fun.
examples: The roller coaster was the tallest ride in the park.
Tickets for each ride cost two coins.
She was too small to go on the spinning ride.

easy.def: A person who rides.
examples: The rider held the reins.
A rider sat on the horse.
The riders raced.

more.def: A person who rides a horse, a bike or other vehicle.
examples: The rider held the reins tightly.
Bike riders wore helmets.
The horse and rider jumped the fence.

easy.def: A long, narrow top of a hill.
examples: We walked along the ridge.
The ridge is high.
Clouds hid the ridge.

more.def: A long, narrow strip of high land, or a raised line on a surface.
examples: We walked along the mountain ridge.
The ridge was covered with snow.
The roof has a ridge along the top.

easy.def: To make fun of someone.
examples: Do not ridicule others.
They ridiculed his idea.
She ridiculed him.

more.def: To laugh at someone or something in a mean way.
examples: It is unkind to ridicule someone's drawing.
The crowd ridiculed his silly idea.
They ridiculed her for wearing a funny hat.

easy.def: Very silly.
examples: He wore a ridiculous hat.
It was a ridiculous idea.
The joke was ridiculous.

more.def: So silly or strange that it makes people laugh.
examples: The clown wore a ridiculous pair of giant shoes.
It is ridiculous to wear a coat in July.
She told a ridiculous story about a flying cow.

easy.def: In a very silly way.
examples: The hat was ridiculously big.
He was ridiculously tall.
The dog looked ridiculously funny.

more.def: In a way that is so silly or extreme that it seems funny.
examples: The hat was ridiculously big for his head.
The line for the ride was ridiculously long.
She was ridiculously happy about the tiny prize.

easy.def: A short, catchy bit of music.
examples: The guitar played a riff.
I hum that riff.
He played a cool riff.

more.def: A short repeated pattern of notes in a song, often played on guitar.
examples: The guitarist played a catchy riff to begin the song.
I can't stop humming that riff.
The drummer joined in on the riff.

easy.def: A long gun.
examples: The museum has an old rifle.
The soldier in the picture holds a rifle.
The rifle is in a glass case.

more.def: A long gun that is held against the shoulder when it is aimed and fired.
examples: The museum has an old rifle from the days of the pioneers.
Hunters and soldiers carry a rifle.
The rifle hangs over the fireplace in the old cabin.

easy.def: Correct, with no mistakes.
examples: Your answer is right.
That is the right way.
I picked the right door.

more.def: Correct or true, or fair and good to do.
examples: You got the right answer on the math problem.
It is right to tell the truth, even when it is hard.
This is the right key for the front door.

easy.def: On the side that is not the left.
examples: Raise your right hand.
Turn right at the corner.
My right shoe is untied.

more.def: On the side of your body that is opposite the side where your heart is.
examples: Drivers in this country stay on the right side of the road.
She held the paintbrush in her right hand.
The library is on your right as you walk in.

easy.def: Good and fair.
examples: She is a righteous person.
He felt righteous.
A righteous king.

more.def: Doing what is right and fair; honest and good.
examples: The righteous king was kind and fair to everyone.
She felt righteous when she told the truth.
He is a righteous man who always helps his neighbors.

easy.def: Being good and fair.
examples: He is known for righteousness.
Righteousness is good.
She acted with righteousness.

more.def: The quality of being morally right, good and fair in how you act.
examples: The judge was known for her righteousness and her fair decisions.
The story honored the hero's righteousness.
Righteousness means doing what is right.

easy.def: Right by law or fairness.
examples: He is the rightful owner.
The rightful king.
The rightful winner.

more.def: Right and fair by law or by what is just.
examples: The lost dog was returned to its rightful owner.
In the story, the prince became the rightful king.
The judge named her the rightful winner of the contest.

easy.def: In a way that is fair and correct.
examples: The prize is rightfully hers.
He rightfully won.
It belongs rightfully to him.

more.def: In a way that is fair, correct or by law.
examples: The medal rightfully belongs to the winner.
She was rightfully proud of her work.
The land rightfully belongs to the family.

easy.def: In the correct way.
examples: She rightly won.
He rightly said no.
You rightly guessed.

more.def: In a way that is fair, correct or true.
examples: She was rightly proud of her work.
He rightly pointed out the mistake.
The team rightly won the cup.

easy.def: A person who uses the right hand more than the left.
examples: I am a righty.
The righty threw the ball.
She is a righty.

more.def: A person who uses the right hand more easily than the left.
examples: I am a righty, so I write with my right hand.
The righty pitcher threw the ball hard.
Most people are righties.

easy.def: Stiff and not bending.
examples: The board is rigid.
A rigid rule.
He stood rigid.

more.def: Stiff and not able to bend, or strict and not willing to change.
examples: The metal pole was rigid and did not bend at all.
She stood rigid with fear.
The teacher had a rigid rule about no talking.

easy.def: To make someone angry or upset.
examples: The noise riled me.
Do not rile the dog.
His joke riled her.

more.def: To make someone annoyed or angry.
examples: The loud noise riled the dog and made it bark.
Do not rile your sister, or she will not play.
The unfair call riled the whole team.

easy.def: The edge of something round.
examples: Fill the cup to the rim.
The ball hit the rim.
Sit on the rim of the bowl.

more.def: The outer edge of something round, such as a cup, a basketball hoop or a wheel.
examples: She filled the glass right to the rim without spilling a drop.
The basketball bounced off the rim and into my hands.
We stood on the rim of the huge crater and looked down.

easy.def: The thick outside skin of a fruit or cheese.
examples: I peeled the rind.
The rind is thick.
The rind of the melon is hard.

more.def: The thick outer skin of fruits such as melons or lemons, or of cheese.
examples: The watermelon rind is thick and green.
She grated lemon rind into the batter.
Dad cut the rind off the cheese.

easy.def: A round band you wear on your finger.
examples: She wears a gold ring.
The ring is too big.
He found a ring in the sand.

more.def: A small circle of metal worn as jewelry on a finger.
examples: She wore a silver ring on her finger.
The ring had a tiny blue stone.
He lost the ring in the grass.

easy.def: A circle.
examples: The kids sat in a ring.
A ring of mushrooms grew here.
Saturn has rings.

more.def: A shape like a circle, or a group standing in a circle.
examples: Saturn is surrounded by rings of ice and dust.
The children stood in a ring and held hands.
A ring of tall trees circled the pond.

easy.def: To make the sound of a bell.
examples: The bell rings at noon.
The phone rang.
I ring the doorbell.

more.def: To make a clear sound like a bell.
examples: The school bell rings at the end of the day.
The phone rang three times before I answered.
Church bells rang across the town.

easy.def: The person who leads a group in doing something naughty.
examples: The ringleader planned a prank.
He was the ringleader.
The ringleader led the way.

more.def: The person who leads others, especially in doing something wrong.
examples: The ringleader planned the silly prank.
The boy was the ringleader of the mischief.
The ringleader gave the signal and the kids ran.

easy.def: A long, curly lock of hair.
examples: She had ringlets.
A ringlet fell on her face.
The ringlet was gold.

more.def: A long, spiral curl of hair.
examples: The girl's hair fell in golden ringlets.
A ringlet bounced on her shoulder.
She curled her hair into ringlets for the party.

easy.def: The person who runs a circus show.
examples: The ringmaster called out.
The ringmaster wore a hat.
The ringmaster waved.

more.def: The person in charge of the acts in a circus ring, who announces them.
examples: The ringmaster introduced each act in a loud voice.
The ringmaster wore a red coat and a tall hat.
The children cheered when the ringmaster appeared.

easy.def: The seats right next to a ring.
examples: We sat ringside.
A ringside seat is close.
Ringside tickets cost more.

more.def: The area or seats right next to a boxing ring or a circus ring.
examples: We had ringside seats at the circus.
The ringside crowd cheered the clown.
A ringside seat lets you see the acrobats up close.

easy.def: A place with ice or a smooth floor for skating.
examples: We skated at the rink.
The rink is cold.
The ice rink is smooth.

more.def: A smooth surface of ice or a floor where people skate or play hockey.
examples: We skated around the ice rink to the sound of music.
The hockey team practiced at the rink on Saturday.
A skating rink was set up in the park for the winter.

easy.def: To wash with clean water to take off soap.
examples: Rinse the dishes.
I rinsed my hands.
Rinse the soap off.

more.def: To wash something lightly with clean water, especially to get rid of soap or dirt.
examples: Rinse the strawberries before you eat them.
She rinsed the soap from her hands under the tap.
After brushing, rinse your mouth with water.

easy.def: A wild, angry crowd.
examples: The riot was loud.
A riot broke out in the street.
The police stopped the riot.

more.def: A violent disturbance by a crowd of people.
examples: A riot broke out in the crowded street.
The police tried to stop the riot.
The story tells of a riot in an old city.

easy.def: A noisy, wild crowd.
examples: The rioting ended.
There was rioting in the street.
The rioting was loud.

more.def: Wild and violent behavior by a crowd.
examples: The rioting ended when police arrived.
There was rioting in the streets.
Fear of rioting closed the shops.

easy.def: To tear.
examples: Do not rip the paper.
I ripped my shirt.
She ripped the card open.

more.def: To tear something quickly or with force.
examples: Be careful not to rip the paper.
He ripped his jeans on the fence.
She ripped open the gift.

easy.def: A tear in something.
examples: There is a rip in my pants.
A rip in the bag.
The rip in the sail is big.

more.def: A long tear in cloth or paper.
examples: There is a rip in my jacket.
Dad sewed up the rip in the tent.
A rip in the sail let the wind through.

easy.def: Ready to eat.
examples: The peach is ripe.
A ripe banana is yellow.
The ripe apples fell.

more.def: Grown and ready to be eaten.
examples: The peach was ripe and juicy.
A ripe banana is yellow and sweet.
We picked the ripe tomatoes from the garden.

easy.def: To become ready to eat.
examples: The fruit will ripen.
The tomatoes ripened.
Bananas ripen fast.

more.def: To become ripe, or ready to be eaten.
examples: The tomatoes ripen in the summer sun.
The bananas ripened on the counter.
Put the fruit in a bag to help it ripen.

easy.def: A small wave on the water.
examples: A ripple spread on the pond.
I saw ripples in the lake.
The stone made a ripple.

more.def: A small wave on the surface of water, or a gentle movement that spreads out.
examples: I dropped a pebble into the pond and watched the ripples spread.
A ripple of laughter went through the class.
The wind made tiny ripples on the lake.

easy.def: To make small waves.
examples: The pond rippled.
The flag rippled.
Water ripples when you drop a stone.

more.def: To form small waves, or to move in little waves.
examples: The surface of the pond rippled when the duck swam by.
The tall grass rippled in the breeze.
The flag rippled in the wind.

easy.def: Making small waves.
examples: The rippling water.
A rippling brook.
The rippling flag waved.

more.def: Forming small, gentle waves.
examples: The rippling water caught the light.
A rippling brook ran through the field.
The rippling flag waved in the breeze.

easy.def: To go up.
examples: The sun rises.
Bread dough rises.
The balloon rose.

more.def: To move up to a higher place.
examples: The sun rises in the east.
Bread dough rises in a warm place.
The balloon rose slowly into the sky.

easy.def: An increase.
examples: There is a rise in the price.
A rise in heat.
The rise of the river.

more.def: A going up in amount or level.
examples: There was a rise in the price of eggs.
A rise in temperature melted the snow.
The rise of the river worried the town.

easy.def: A person who gets up, or the upright part of a stair.
examples: He is an early riser.
The stair riser is short.
I am a late riser.

more.def: A person who gets up at a certain time, or the upright part of a step.
examples: Dad is an early riser who wakes at five.
The riser of each step is painted white.
She is a late riser on weekends.

easy.def: A chance that something bad may happen.
examples: There is a risk of rain.
Climbing is a risk.
Skating on thin ice is a risk.

more.def: The chance that something bad or dangerous could happen.
examples: There is a risk of rain on Saturday.
Climbing a tall ladder has some risk.
Divers know the risks of deep water.

easy.def: To do something that may be dangerous.
examples: He risked getting wet.
She risked a fall.
They risked the storm.

more.def: To do something even though something bad might happen.
examples: He risked slipping on the icy path.
She risked missing the bus to help a friend.
The firefighter risked her safety to save the kitten.

easy.def: Likely to cause harm.
examples: The icy hill is risky.
It is risky to swim alone.
That is a risky jump.

more.def: Dangerous or likely to go wrong.
examples: Climbing the loose rocks was a risky choice.
The rope bridge looked risky.
Skating on thin ice is a risky thing to do.

easy.def: A special ceremony that is done the same way each time.
examples: The rite is done at noon.
A rite of passage.
The rite is old.

more.def: A formal act or ceremony, often a religious or traditional one.
examples: The old rite is done at noon each year.
Getting your first tooth pulled is a rite of passage.
Rites such as weddings are important in every culture.

easy.def: Something people do the same way each time.
examples: Our bedtime ritual is a story and a song.
Pancakes on Sunday are a family ritual.
The team has a ritual before each game.

more.def: A set of actions done in the same way each time, often for a special reason or on a special day.
examples: The class has a morning ritual of greeting each person by name.
Lighting candles is a ritual in many holiday celebrations.
Brushing his teeth and reading a book was his nightly ritual.

easy.def: A person you compete against.
examples: The rival team won.
He is my rival.
The two rivals shook hands.

more.def: A person or team that tries to beat you in a contest.
examples: Our rival team won the game.
The rival schools meet in the finals each year.
He is my rival in the spelling bee.

easy.def: A friendly or tough contest between two teams.
examples: The two teams have a rivalry.
There is a rivalry between the towns.
The rivalry is fun.

more.def: A competition between people or teams who each want to be the best.
examples: The two schools have a friendly rivalry in sports.
Their rivalry made every game exciting.
The rivalry between the two towns goes back many years.

easy.def: A long stream of water that flows to the sea.
examples: The river is wide.
There is a boat on the river.
We fish in the river.

more.def: A large stream of water that flows across the land into a sea, a lake or a bigger stream.
examples: The river winds through the valley.
Ducks swam down the river.
We crossed the river on a bridge.

easy.def: The land beside a river.
examples: We sat on the riverbank.
The riverbank is muddy.
Ducks walked on the riverbank.

more.def: The land along the edge of a river.
examples: We sat on the riverbank and watched the boats.
The riverbank was muddy after the rain.
Willow trees grew along the riverbank.

easy.def: The ground at the bottom of a river.
examples: The riverbed was dry.
Stones lay on the riverbed.
We walked on the riverbed.

more.def: The ground at the bottom of a river or stream.
examples: The riverbed was dry in summer.
Smooth stones lay on the riverbed.
A fish swam above the sandy riverbed.

easy.def: The land beside a river.
examples: We picnicked at the riverside.
The riverside is green.
They walked at the riverside.

more.def: The land along the edge of a river.
examples: We had a picnic at the riverside.
A path ran along the riverside.
Willow trees grew at the riverside.

easy.def: A metal pin used to hold metal pieces together.
examples: The bridge has rivets.
A rivet holds the plates.
The rivet is metal.

more.def: A short metal pin used to join pieces of metal tightly together.
examples: Workers hammered rivets into the steel beams.
The old ship was held together with thousands of rivets.
Jeans have small metal rivets at the pockets.

easy.def: To hold your attention.
examples: The story riveted me.
The game riveted us.
The show riveted the crowd.

more.def: To hold someone's attention completely.
examples: The magic show riveted the audience.
The story of the shipwreck riveted the whole class.
The movie riveted him from start to finish.
